author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
body: initialQuery now calls quoteIdentifierIfNecessary(vars[0]). If there are no non-expression queries, refIds can be empty (ExpressionQueryEditor filters out the current query), making vars[0] undefined and causing a runtime crash when quoteIdentifierIfNecessary runs. Add a guard for the empty refIds/vars case (e.g., don’t generate an initial FROM clause / use a placeholder and skip auto-initialization) and add a regression test for mounting SqlExpr with an empty refIds array.

body: quoteIdentifierIfNecessary (from MySQL sqlUtil) is not idempotent: if a query name/refId is already wrapped in backticks (a plausible workaround users may already have saved), it will get wrapped again and produce invalid SQL. Consider unquoting first (e.g., via unquoteIdentifier) or adding an explicit “already quoted” check before re-quoting.

author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
body: Table quoting logic is inconsistent across the SQL expressions feature: this file uses the local quoteIdentifierIfNecessary (regex-only) while SqlExpr/autocomplete use the MySQL sqlUtil version (which also quotes reserved words). This can lead to cases where the editor generates a quoted FROM clause but the schema/fields metadata query still uses an unquoted table name (e.g., refId like "TABLE"). Use a single shared quoting helper for all SQL-expressions table/field quoting (and ideally handle reserved words + already-quoted identifiers).
admission_reason: line inside a changed hunk at the checkpoint
matchable_reason: Both implementations coexist at the checkpoint exactly as described: metaSqlExpr.ts:114 defines a local regex-only quoteIdentifierIfNecessary used at metaSqlExpr.ts:15, while SqlExpr.tsx:13 and sqlCompletionProvider.ts:9 import the reserved-word-aware sqlUtil version.
thread_group_defect: Two different quoting implementations are used inside the SQL-expressions feature - the local regex-only helper at metaSqlExpr.ts:114 versus the reserved-word-aware sqlUtil version used by SqlExpr and the completion provider - so the FROM clause and the schema/fields metadata query can disagree on whether a table name is quoted.

author: NWRichmond
body:
I'm concerned about this dependency on a plugin, especially because many data source plugins are in the process of being externalized (decoupled from core Grafana, versioned independently, living in another repo). I'm not sure if the MySQL data source is one of them, but we should be careful.
Perhaps there's a need for utilities like these to be exposed via @grafana/sql, which could then be used here and in app/plugins/datasource/mysql/sqlUtil.ts (and perhaps elsewhere, like influxdb/fsql/sqlUtil.ts, although this requires double-quotes instead of backticks).

author: cursor
body:
Reserved keyword used as placeholder
Medium Severity

When there are no refIds, the seeded SQL expression uses the unquoted placeholder table. TABLE is reserved in the MySQL-compatible backend, so FROM table fails at parse time instead of producing a clearer missing-table error. This shows up whenever a SQL expression is created with no source queries yet.
